title: Heavy-light decomposition (HLD)
relevance: Medium — OAs almost never ask for a full HLD template, but “path / subtree update+query on a tree” is the CF skill that separates “knows Euler tour” from Candidate Master tree DS; Striver never covers it.
company_notes: Almost never “implement HLD”; org-chart path metrics (sum/max on manager chain with salary updates) expect Euler or binary lifting first, HLD when constraints force it. Network/cable: edge latency update + path delay (ABC294 G / Path Queries II — edge on child + path sum). Subtree broadcast + path reset (Water Tree) often Euler+lazy in interviews. Recognition gate: why path-max-with-updates is harder than subtree-sum (contiguous tour vs O(log n) chain pieces).

phases.goal: Map path/subtree update+query wording to HLD versus Euler, tree-diff, or binary lifting.

must_hit.point: Signal words: path max/min under updates, paint path then query, path + subtree mixed updates, function composition along a path.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists those signals and reaches for HLD rather than Euler-only or static lifting.

must_hit.point: Use HLD for arbitrary path aggregates with updates (max/min/sum/composite) that Euler+BIT alone cannot do — e.g. path max with point updates.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names updates + non-trivial path aggregates and cites path max with point updates as the Euler+BIT gap.

must_hit.point: Prefer Euler / tree-diff / binary lifting when queries are only subtree, only root→node, or path sum without awkward ops.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Declines HLD for subtree-only, root→node sum, or uncomplicated path sum shapes.

must_hit.point: Recognition gate: path-max-with-updates is harder than subtree-sum because subtrees are contiguous tour ranges while a path breaks into O(log n) chain pieces.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Contrasts contiguous [tin,tout]-style ranges with O(log n) chain segments on a path.

probes: What wording makes you reach for HLD instead of Euler tour or binary lifting?
Why is path-max-with-updates harder than subtree-sum?

hints.1: Ask whether you need path aggregates under updates, or only subtree / root→node / static path ops.
hints.2: Signals are path max/min under updates, paint-then-query, path+subtree mix, path composition; skip HLD for subtree-only, root→node sum, or plain path sum.
hints.3: Say: HLD when updates + non-trivial path aggregates (e.g. path max + point updates) beat Euler+BIT; prefer Euler/tree-diff/lifting otherwise; path-max is harder because a path is O(log n) chain pieces, not one contiguous tour range.

phases.goal: Define heavy/light edges, chains, heavy-first layout, and the light-edge path bound.

must_hit.point: Root the tree; mark the child with largest subtree as heavy, others light; heavy edges form disjoint chains.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Defines heavy = largest sz[child], light = the rest, and chains as contiguous heavy-edge paths.

must_hit.point: Assign contiguous segment-tree indices along each chain via heavy-first DFS so each subtree stays a contiguous [tin, tout]-style range.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names heavy-first DFS and contiguous chain (and subtree) index blocks.

must_hit.point: Light-edge lemma: each light step halves subtree size ⇒ any root→v path has O(log n) light edges ⇒ O(log n) chains on any u–v path.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States the halving argument and O(log n) light edges / chain segments on a path.

must_hit.point: With a segtree, each path query/update is O(log^2 n) because you query O(log n) chain segments.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Multiplies O(log n) segments by segtree cost to get O(log^2 n) per path op.

probes: How do you choose the heavy child, and what do heavy edges form?
Why does any u–v path touch only O(log n) chains?

hints.1: Start from largest-subtree child as heavy, then think about chains and light jumps.
hints.2: Heavy-first DFS lays chains contiguously; each light edge halves sz ⇒ O(log n) lights/chains on a path.
hints.3: Say: heavy = max sz[child], light otherwise; heavy edges → disjoint chains with contiguous segtree indices (heavy-first DFS); light steps halve size ⇒ O(log n) chains on u–v ⇒ O(log^2 n) path ops with a segtree.

phases.goal: Spell head/pos fields, the climb-head path loop, edge-on-child storage, and free subtree ranges.

must_hit.point: Heavy child = largest sz[child]; head[v] = top of v’s chain; pos[v] = index in the single segtree; decompose the heavy child first so chains and subtrees are contiguous.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names sz, head, pos, and heavy-first decomposition order.

must_hit.point: Path query loop: while head[u] != head[v], lift the deeper head, segtree-query [pos[head], pos[node]], jump to parent[head]; then query the final same-chain segment.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Walks the climb-head[] loop and the final same-chain query.

must_hit.point: Edge values: store edge (p,v)’s weight at v; on path u–v exclude the LCA vertex when summing edge weights.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Puts edge weight on the child vertex and excludes LCA on edge-path queries.

must_hit.point: With heavy-first ordering, subtree(v) = [pos[v], pos[v]+sz[v]) — same HLD array handles path and subtree.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Gives the half-open subtree range on the HLD pos array.

probes: What do head[] and pos[] store, and why decompose the heavy child first?
Walk me through the climb-head path query loop.
How do you store edge weights and query a path sum of edges?

hints.1: Fields are head (chain top) and pos (segtree index); climb until heads match.
hints.2: Heavy-first so ranges stay contiguous; while heads differ, query deeper chain then jump to parent[head]; edges live on the child vertex.
hints.3: Say: head[v]/pos[v], heavy-first; while head[u]!=head[v] lift deeper head, query [pos[head],pos[node]], jump parent[head], then same-chain segment; edge (p,v) at v and exclude LCA; subtree = [pos[v], pos[v]+sz[v]).

phases.goal: State the O(log n) chain bound and the O((n+q) log^2 n) target with a segtree.

must_hit.point: Any u–v path crosses O(log n) light edges and therefore O(log n) chain segments.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States O(log n) light edges and O(log n) chain pieces per path.

must_hit.point: Each path query/update is O(log^2 n) with a segtree (O(log n) segments × segtree cost).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Gives O(log^2 n) per path operation with one segtree.

must_hit.point: Complexity target: O((n+q) log^2 n) with one segtree, or O((n+q) log n) with specialized tricks.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States both the log^2 target and the specialized log trick bound from the checklist.

probes: Why is a path query O(log^2 n) rather than O(log n)?
What total complexity do you quote for n nodes and q path updates/queries?

hints.1: Count how many chain pieces a path hits, then multiply by segtree cost.
hints.2: O(log n) chains × O(log n) segtree ⇒ O(log^2 n) per op; overall O((n+q) log^2 n).
hints.3: Say: O(log n) light edges/chains on any path; path op O(log^2 n) with one segtree; target O((n+q) log^2 n), or O((n+q) log n) with specialized tricks.

phases.goal: Catch LCA exclusion on edges, non-commutative path folds, overusing HLD, and integer overflow.

must_hit.point: When edges live on child vertices, exclude the LCA carefully on the final same-chain segment (and when summing edge weights on u–v).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Calls out LCA exclusion for edge-on-child path queries in the climb loop.

must_hit.point: Non-commutative monoids (composites): split the path at LCA into up-going and down-going folds; maintain reverse merge or two segtrees.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Splits at LCA and mentions reverse merge / two trees for ax+b-style composition.

must_hit.point: Do not reach for HLD when simpler tools suffice: subtree only → Euler; root→node sum → Euler difference; offline path += → tree diff + LCA; static path min/max → binary lifting.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists those four escape hatches before writing HLD.

must_hit.point: Always use long long on CF/AtCoder distances.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions long long for distance / path sums on those platforms.

probes: What goes wrong if you include the LCA when edge weights sit on child vertices?
How do you fold a non-commutative function composition along u→v?
When is HLD the wrong hammer?

hints.1: Check edge-vs-vertex storage, whether the monoid commutes, and whether a simpler tree tool fits.
hints.2: Exclude LCA for edges-on-child; split composites at LCA with reverse/two trees; prefer Euler/tree-diff/lifting when the query shape allows.
hints.3: Say: store edge (p,v) at v and exclude LCA; non-commutative → up/down from LCA with reverse merge or two segtrees; skip HLD for subtree-only, root→node sum, offline path +=, or static path min/max; use long long on CF/AtCoder distances.

tradeoffs.strong_answer: Subtree-only PURS or lazy subtree flips → Euler (+ Fenwick/lazy); tin/tout is the mental model HLD reuses, but skip chains when you never need arbitrary path pieces under updates.

tradeoffs.topic: HLD vs Euler path-to-root / tree difference
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Root→node sum with updates → Euler tour difference; offline path += 1 → tree difference + LCA. HLD is overkill for those shapes; reach for HLD when updates mix with non-trivial path aggregates (e.g. path max).
Static path min/max (no updates) → binary lifting. HLD when path aggregates must support updates (point set + path maximum, edge update + path distance).

tradeoffs.topic: Commutative path aggregates vs non-commutative path composites
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Sum/max along a path can climb chains in one segtree. Non-commutative composition (ax+b u→v) needs a split at LCA into up-going and down-going folds with reverse merge or two segtrees.

gotchas.trap: Including the LCA vertex when edge weights are stored on child vertices.
gotchas.correction: Store edge (p,v)’s weight at v; on path u–v exclude the LCA when summing edge weights, and exclude LCA carefully on the final same-chain segment.

gotchas.trap: Treating a non-commutative path fold like a commutative sum/max climb.
gotchas.correction: Split at LCA into up-going and down-going folds; maintain reverse merge or two segtrees (Vertex Set Path Composite style).

gotchas.trap: Reaching for HLD on subtree-only, root→node sum, offline path increments, or static path min/max.
gotchas.correction: Use Euler; Euler difference; tree diff + LCA; or binary lifting respectively — HLD when updates + non-trivial path aggregates mix.

gotchas.trap: Using 32-bit ints for path distances on CF/AtCoder.
gotchas.correction: Always use long long on CF/AtCoder distances.
